newsitem.title: FRANCE: Two hurt in bomb attack on Corsica gendarmes.
newsitem.headline: Two hurt in bomb attack on Corsica gendarmes.

text.p: Suspected separatist guerrillas bombed and machinegunned a gendarmerie barracks in Corsica on Friday, sending a gendarme and a woman into shock, police said.
Two gunmen on a motorbike hurled a bomb and fired 16 bullets at the barracks, at Ghisonaccia on the Mediterranean island's east coast.
Police said the sentry on duty suffered shock and hearing injuries from the blast. The wife of a gendarme, who was outside the barracks, was also in shock.
It was the first time injuries were reported in a recent spate of attacks on paramilitary gendarmerie targets on the French Mediterranean island.

The attack bore the hallmarks of the outlawed Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC)-Historic Wing, which has claimed responsibility for nine bombings or machinegunnings on the holiday island in the past week.
The FLNC, which has also carried out bombings on the French mainland recently, has threatened to step up its campaign and warned families of gendarmes on the island to return to mainland France.
The FLNC said earlier this week it was "at war" with the gendarmes.
A FLNC guerrilla was believed to have been wounded when gendarmes opened fire during a drive-by attack on another barracks. Blood stains were found in the abandoned car.
The latest attack followed the arrest of Corsica's best-known separatist leader Francois Santoni who was remanded in custody in Paris on Wednesday.
Santoni, head of Cuncolta Naziunalista, the FLNC's legal wing, and his lawyer girlfriend Marie-Helene Mattei were placed under investigation for attempted extortion and bomb attacks.

The separatist group issued a statement on Friday accusing the government of fabricating one of the allegations against the pair -- that they were linked to an extortion attempt against the owner of an island golf course.
The course caretaker's home was blown up, and the owner said the bombing took place after he refused to pay protection money demanded by the separatists.
"There is no evidence for this. Our militants are the object of a relentless high-profile political campaign aimed at destabilising the nationalist movement," the FLNC said.
